question: For the constraints $x+y\le7$, $x+3y\le12$, $x\ge0$ and $y\ge0$, a family of proposed solutions is given by $Q(t,t+1)$, where $t\ge0$. Determine exactly the values of $t$ for which $Q$ becomes an infeasible solution and justify the limiting value by checking all the constraints.
explanation:
Verification of the Constraints
For $Q(t,t+1)$ with $t\ge0$, both coordinates are non-negative, so the non-negative restrictions are automatically satisfied. Substituting in $x+y\le7$ gives $$t+(t+1)\le7,$$ so $2t+1\le7$ and hence $t\le3$. Substituting in $x+3y\le12$ gives $$t+3(t+1)\le12,$$ so $4t+3\le12$ and hence $t\le\frac{9}{4}$.

For a point to be feasible, both restrictions must hold simultaneously. Therefore, with $t\ge0$, $Q$ is feasible when $$0\le t\le\frac{9}{4}.$$ At the limiting value $t=\frac{9}{4}$, we have $x+y=\frac{11}{2}\le7$ and $x+3y=12$, so the point still satisfies all the constraints and is feasible.

For every $t>\frac{9}{4}$, $4t+3>12$, and hence the constraint $x+3y\le12$ is violated. Therefore such a point is infeasible. For $t>3$, the constraint $x+y\le7$ is also violated, but violation of even one constraint is sufficient to make a solution infeasible.

Final Result
$Q(t,t+1)$ is a feasible solution for $0\le t\le\frac{9}{4}$ and is an infeasible solution for every $t>\frac{9}{4}$.

options.A: $Q(t,t+1)$ is infeasible for $t\geq\frac{9}{4}$; the limiting point is also infeasible
options.B: $Q(t,t+1)$ is feasible for $0\leq t\leq\frac{9}{4}$ and infeasible for $t>\frac{9}{4}$
options.C: $Q(t,t+1)$ is feasible for $0\leq t\leq3$ and infeasible only for $t>3$
